text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Beijing reiterates its message that Japan should take steps to remove a lighthouse built by a Japanese right-wing group on disputed islands in the East China Sea.
- Japan calls for more confidence-building among countries in the region and greater transparency in policy-making.
- The U.S. may consider taking action against Malaysia's state oil company Petronas after its involvement in Iran, legislative director for U.S. senator says.
- Many Singapore schools introduce "eye-robic" programmes to help reduce students' eyestrain.
- Number of millionaires in Singapore almost triples in four years to 1994, from 143 in 1991 to 386 in 1994.
- Ninety percent of Singapore's corporate taxes contributed by 2.5 percent of the 80,000 registered companies in 1994.
- Housing Board flats contributed only two percent of Singapore's property taxes in fiscal year ended March 31.
- Former star trader of world copper market, Yasuo Hamanaka, admits he forged documents relating to Sumitomo Corp's multi-billion dollar trading losses, one of his lawyers says.
- Canadian mining company, Bre-X Minerals Ltd, forges strategic alliance with President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, granting him stake potentially worth Canadian $609 million.
- Fashion group FJ Benjamin Holdings, which launched initial public offer on Tuesday, given Central Provident Fund trustee stock status, in first instance of such status being granted since 1994.
- Contractors face problems delivering projects on time after recent crackdown on illegal foreign construction workers.
- Malaysia's YTL Corp chief Francis Yeoh says firm will not bid for Hongkong-listed Consolidated Electric Power Asia after failing to secure irrevocable undertaking from major shareholder Gordon Wu.
- Uraco Holdings wants controlling stake in US-based Longs Mfg Inc to expand base to machine suppliers in wafer fabrication and medical equipment industries.
- Singapore Airline shares slide on selling from United Kingdom, United States.
